title: MZ Can anyone help me make sense of why my VisuStella plugins are suddenly returning this fatal error?

posts.author: coldtyrant
posts.body:
This screen occurs whenever I attempt to use the Random Dungeon Maps to generate the Map templates for an empty container.
The plugin worked perfectly all day, until suddenly it didn't.
Usually the culprit would be - installing an incompatible plugin, removing a plugin, changing the plugin load order, etc., but I did none of these things.
Additionally, I did not delete any files from my Project folder.
Suddenly - for a reason I cannot discern - the Random Dungeon Maps no longer works and returns a "Cannot read property 'parentId' of null".
Completely uninstalling and reinstalling the plugin did not work.
Despite the fact it worked with all my other plugins previously, I uninstalled every plugin except VisuMZ Core Engine and Random Dungeon Maps, but the error still persisted.
I created a New Project and then installed only VisuMZ Core Engine and Random Dungeon Maps, and the error DID NOT happen. However, starting my entire Project over from scratch is clearly not an option.
Something has somehow broken, and I'm hoping someone can help me figure this out. I'm unfortunately at a loss and may need to abandon the plugin.
(Apologies if I posted this in the wrong forum section.)

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
you need to understand what the error truly means - the causes you listed are not the only options that can have this effect.
"of null" and "of undefined" always means that the engine tried to access a data object that does not exist.
why it does not exist that can be a lot of reasons like a plugin configuration or incompatibility.
but it can be caused by other options as well, like simply deleting a database entry that is required by the plugin or something similar.
since it works with a new project, you'll have to compare that with your existing project to find out what the missing data object might be - a missing map, a missing entry in the database or even something as simple as a missing notetag or a notetag pointing nowhere.

posts.author: coldtyrant
posts.body:
I figured out the problem. Thankfully, this was user error, and nothing was corrupted or broken.
This was my MapInfos.json:
As you can see, it's absolutely littered with null entries. These were from Maps I deleted.
The actual Maps have several fields, one of them being a parentId.
"Cannot read property parentId of null", means the Plugin was trying to read one of the null entries which has no data, and no parentId field like a normal Map does.
It took some work, but I totally reset my MapInfos.json by deleting everything, but preserving the individual Map.json files to copy and paste them onto the fresh maps I made.
My new MapInfos.json no longer has any null entries and my VisuStella Random Dungeon Maps plugin is now working correctly.
A word of advice to anyone that may stumble upon this thread in the future, please be careful when deleting Maps you may no longer want.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
In the plugin properties, the leading zero in front of the map ID - is that an automated format or did you enter it manually?
IDs should NEVER be entered with leading zeroes, the true ID is 59 and not 059.
A single zero should not cause problems unless something is programmed very wrong, but for example 0059 is an undefined number - because 00 causes all computers to read the number as octal, and there is no 9 in octal numbers...
EDIT: OK, it was something else. But as I said further above - a missing data entry...

Oh, it's actually far worse than I thought. I made my previous comment after trying it in the console to make sure, but it turns out it
sometimes
interprets 0-prefixed numbers as octal, and sometimes not.
Instead of raising an error for
059
(because 9 is not a valid octal digit), it just parses it as decimal instead.
It parses
010
as 8, but
Number('010')
or
parseInt('010')
or
+'010'
as 10. (Though, oddly, a StackOverflow I found said that
parseInt
does
auto-detect octal? Maybe it depends on the version, but it does parse to 10 in MV.)
But, all things considered, the latter fact still means that you don't need to worry about this when putting values into note tags or numeric plugin parameters. It's something to worry about in formulas and script calls though.
With
"use strict"
it's a fair bit better – anything 0-prefixed is an error, no questions asked. That's only for literals – string to number conversion is the same. Though honestly I would've preferred if they were parsed as decimal instead.
